body:
Essentially, within Cython we access the options through `Cython.Compiler.Options.optionsInThread`. That looks them up from the existing public `Cython.Compiler.Options` interface but makes changes to the options thread-local. This keeps the original user-facing interface, but uses a safer way of accessing it internally.

The main option that we were changing dynamically was `cimport_from_pyx` (for the shared module, and possibly in another place too).

This'll probably fix most of #7997 although I do wonder if we should protect it more strongly from being run in multiple threads.

I tried an alternative version where I copied all the options to `CompilationOptions` and tried to access them in from the context, but there were too many places I couldn't relibaly get to the context so I abandoned this.

comment_data.body: This (and a few other places) aren't great because they're resolved at import-time so you can't change them after `MemoryView.py` has been imported. But I'm not trying to fix that here.

An alternative version would be to try to make the `Cython.Compiler.Options` scope thread-local and keep exactly the same interface, but that seemed trickier (you have to somehow swap the type of the module after creation)

commit.message:
Make `Cython.Compiler.Options` thread local

Essentially, within Cython we access the options through
`Cython.Compiler.Options.optionsInThread`. That looks them up
from the existing public `Cython.Compiler.Options` interface
but makes changes to the options thread-local. This keeps
the original user-facing interface, but uses a safer way of
accessing it internally.

The main option that we were changing dynamically was `cimport_from_pyx`
(for the shared module, and possibly in another place too).

This'll probably fix most of #7997 although I do wonder if we
should protect it more strongly from being run in multiple threads.

I tried an alternative version where I copied all the options
to `CompilationOptions` and tried to access them in from the
context, but there were too many places I couldn't relibaly get
to the context so I abandoned this.
Remove lookup that shouldn't be there
